details:
POTYZHNI DONBASSYATA is developing an interactive platform for exploring long-term changes in Earth's climate system using NASA Earth science data.

The project allows users to select an environmental variable, such as near-surface air temperature or precipitation, choose a geographical region, and examine how the selected variable has changed over time. The platform presents the results through time-series charts and an interactive 3D globe, helping users connect statistical findings with their geographical context.

The analytical component calculates the direction and rate of change and evaluates whether an observed trend is statistically significant. We use methods such as linear regression, the Mann-Kendall test, and Sen's slope. This approach helps users distinguish long-term trends from random fluctuations and compare environmental changes across different regions.

Our intended impact is to make complex Earth science data more accessible and understandable. The platform can support students, educators, and anyone interested in climate research by turning raw scientific datasets into visual and interpretable information.

The project combines Python-based data processing and statistical analysis with interactive visualization technologies. Our planned software stack includes Python, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall, Streamlit, and Plotly. We use NASA data sources, including NASA POWER, for environmental observations and model-based datasets.

The creative aspect of the project is the combination of statistical trend detection with an interactive globe. Instead of presenting climate change as a single global number, we aim to show how trends vary from one geographical area to another. During development, we considered data reliability, the length of observation periods, seasonal variation, statistical significance, geographical resolution, and ease of use for people without a scientific programming background.
